cards.text: Hosea, a prophet of the LORD, tells this one himself, and friend, it's a heavy one. His wife is loved by another man, and she's an adulteress. Then the LORD speaks to Hosea.

cards.question: Hosea's wife is loved by another man. What does the LORD tell Hosea to do about her?

answers.text: Go show love to her again
Let her go her own way
Send her back to her family

cards.text: AGAIN? After ALL that? Hosea, I'd have dropped a whole tray of cookies right there. But God isn't done. He tells Hosea exactly what kind of love this is.

cards.question: The LORD tells Hosea to love his wife the way the LORD loves the ___, even though they turn to other gods.

cards.text: And God says the Israelites love to offer raisin cakes to idols. Raisin cakes. To a STATUE. As a baker, I'm offended on behalf of every oven I've ever met.
So Hosea goes. He doesn't just ask her to come home. He buys her back.

cards.question: Hosea buys back his wife for fifteen shekels of ___ and some barley.

cards.text: Fifteen shekels and barley. Me? Mother Miller pulled me out of a closing-sale bin for 25 cents. A QUARTER. Then Hosea sits his wife down and tells her how it's going to be.

cards.question: Hosea tells his wife she must live with him for many days. What must she not do?
Hosea asks this of his wife but promises nothing in return.

cards.text: Remember, the LORD said to love her as He loves the Israelites. Now that line about many days comes back, and this time it's about the Israelites.

cards.question: For many days, what will the Israelites live without?

cards.text: No king, no prince. No sacrifice or sacred pillar either.

cards.question: During those many days, Israel will still have its ephod and its idols.

cards.text: But Hosea isn't done. There's an afterward, and friend, an afterward is like opening the oven when you forgot to set the timer. You just don't know yet.

cards.question: After those many days, the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God.
Israel will seek the LORD their God and ___ their king.

cards.text: That's David, king over Israel long before Hosea's day (2 Samuel 5:3). And Hosea says, "They will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the last days."

findings.problem: The passage starts mid-thought: the LORD says to show love to your wife "again." The opening card doesn't say who the wife is or that Hosea married her earlier. Card 3's "After ALL that?" then points back to events this lesson never tells.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The story card runs five sentences ("AGAIN? After ALL that? Hosea, I'd have dropped... But God isn't done. He tells Hosea..."), well past the limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card runs four sentences ("And God says... Raisin cakes. To a STATUE. As a baker..."), past the limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Hosea 3:1 says the raisin cakes are offered "to idols." The card calls the idol "a STATUE," which renames what the text names. Verse 3:4 lists the idol separately from the "sacred pillar," so the text doesn't say what form the idols take.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story card runs three sentences ("So Hosea goes. He doesn't just ask her to come home. He buys her back."), past the limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card runs five sentences or fragments ("Fifteen shekels and barley. Me? Mother Miller... A QUARTER. Then Hosea sits..."), past the limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The first sentence ("Remember, the LORD said to love her as He loves the Israelites.") restates card 4 instead of moving the passage forward.

The comparison is opening the oven after forgetting the timer, which suggests an outcome that might be burnt or ruined. The "afterward" in Hosea 3:5 is a hopeful return to the LORD. The core action doesn't match, and the joke doesn't click without explaining. The card also runs three sentences.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
